gen-01-criador.title: Who created the world?
gen-01-criador.intro: Genesis 1 opens with a powerful declaration: God is the Creator of all. Before anything existed, God already was. Let's start here.
gen-01-criador.centralInsight: God is the center, not me
gen-01-criador.objective: Leave knowing that God begins creation; the void is not a god; the Spirit is already present.
gen-01-criador.hookNote: Before anything existed, God already was. The Bible does not begin with man—it begins with the Creator.

gen-02-dias.title: The days of creation
gen-02-dias.intro: God created the world in six days, each with a purpose. Observe the order: first the environments, then the inhabitants.
gen-02-dias.objective: Why does the order of days matter?
gen-02-dias.hookNote: God organizes chaos in six days: first the environments, then the inhabitants. There is order, rhythm and kindness.
gen-02-dias.echoQuestion: God is the center. What does He do with the chaos?

gen-03-imagem.title: Image of God
gen-03-imagem.intro: In the ancient East, “image of the god” was the title of kings. Genesis gives this to man and woman—all humanity.
gen-03-imagem.centralInsight: Human dignity is not an achievement: it is present — man and woman, under God, with responsibility.
gen-03-imagem.objective: What does it mean to be made in the image of God?
gen-03-imagem.hookNote: The human being is not an accident. It carries the image of God — dignity, responsibility and communion.
gen-03-imagem.echoQuestion: There is order in the days. What does man enter this picture as?

gen-04-descanso.title: God's rest
gen-04-descanso.intro: On the seventh day, God rested. Not because I was tired, but to establish a sacred rhythm of work and rest.
gen-04-descanso.objective: What does rest reveal about God?
gen-04-descanso.hookNote: God's rest is not fatigue—it is completing, sanctifying, and inviting humanity into a rhythm of grace.
gen-04-descanso.echoQuestion: The image is present. Is the seventh day a rest from tiredness — or from a completed work?

gen-boss-01.title: Challenge: Creation
gen-boss-01.intro: Time to prove what you learned about Creation. Take a deep breath — you can do it!
gen-boss-01.objective: What is the center of the creation narrative?
gen-boss-01.hookNote: Review the thread of Creation: God speaks, commands, blesses and rests. Are you ready for the challenge?

gen-05-eden.title: Eden
gen-05-eden.intro: Genesis 2 zooms in on the sixth day: God plants a garden and puts man there to cultivate and keep it.
gen-05-eden.objective: What does the garden teach about human purpose?
gen-05-eden.hookNote: Eden is a place of communion, work and beauty. Man was not made for idleness — he was made to care.
gen-05-eden.echoQuestion: God completes what he begins. What was man made for in the garden?

gen-06-queda.title: The disobedience
gen-06-queda.intro: The serpent tempts Eve, and disobedience enters the world. A moment that changes all of human history.
gen-06-queda.objective: Where does distrust begin in the story?
gen-06-queda.hookNote: Temptation begins by distorting the word of God. Distrusting God opens the door to disobedience.
gen-06-queda.echoQuestion: There is work and communion in Eden. What comes between man and the word of God?

gen-07-consequencias.title: The consequences
gen-07-consequencias.intro: Disobedience brings consequences: guilt, shame, expulsion — but also the first promise of redemption.
gen-07-consequencias.objective: What hope is there after the fall?
gen-07-consequencias.hookNote: Sin breaks relationships: with God, with oneself, with others and with creation. Still, there is promise.
gen-07-consequencias.echoQuestion: The word has been distorted. After disobedience, is there only judgment left?

gen-boss-02.title: Challenge: The Fall
gen-boss-02.intro: Test your knowledge about Eden and the Fall. Let's go!
gen-boss-02.objective: How does the fall prepare the history of salvation?
gen-boss-02.hookNote: The challenge of the Fall requires seeing the contrast: the perfect garden and the need for redemption.

gen-08-caim.title: Cain and Abel
gen-08-caim.intro: Outside of Eden, sin intensifies. Cain kills Abel — the first murder in history.
gen-08-caim.objective: What does Cain's story reveal about the human heart?
gen-08-caim.hookNote: Sin progresses: from disobedience to violence. God still confronts and offers a way.
gen-08-caim.echoQuestion: Sin has a cost. Where does he go from here?

gen-09-diluvio.title: The flood and Noah
gen-09-diluvio.intro: Evil grows in the land. God judges the world but preserves Noah and his family—a new beginning.
gen-09-diluvio.objective: How do grace and judgment appear together in the flood?
gen-09-diluvio.hookNote: Judgment and grace go together: the flood confronts evil; the covenant promises God's faithfulness.
gen-09-diluvio.echoQuestion: From disobedience to violence. Do judgment and grace still go together?

gen-10-babel.title: Tower of Babel
gen-10-babel.intro: Humanity unites to make itself famous. God confuses languages ​​and scatters peoples.
gen-10-babel.objective: What does Babel say about godless ambition?
gen-10-babel.hookNote: Babel is collective pride: making a name without God. The confusion of languages ​​limits human arrogance.
gen-10-babel.echoQuestion: God takes sin seriously. Does human pride still try another path?

gen-11-abraao.title: Abraham's Call
gen-11-abraao.intro: Genesis 12 changes course: God calls Abram to a journey of faith and promise—the beginning of Israel's history.
gen-11-abraao.objective: Why does Abram's call change history?
gen-11-abraao.hookNote: After the judgment and confusion, God calls a man — and through him promises blessing to all families.
gen-11-abraao.echoQuestion: Babel scattered the families. Does God abandon them — or call someone?

gen-boss-final.title: Final Challenge: Genesis 1–11
gen-boss-final.intro: Last challenge of this journey. Show everything you learned!
gen-boss-final.objective: What is the thread that connects Creation, Fall and Abraham?
gen-boss-final.hookNote: This challenge ties together the thread of Genesis 1–11. You're not just testing memory—you're laying out God's plan.

gen12-01-chamado.title: Abram's Call
gen12-01-chamado.intro: He leaves his land, his relatives and his father's house — the promise begins with a step of faith.
gen12-01-chamado.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-01-chamado.objective: What does Abram leave behind—and what does God promise ahead?
gen12-01-chamado.hookNote: He leaves his land, his relatives and his father's house — the promise begins with a step of faith.

gen12-02-egito-e-lot.title: Egypt and Lot's separation
gen12-02-egito-e-lot.intro: Hunger takes Abram to Egypt; later, he and Lot part ways—Abram keeps the promise, Lot chooses the plain.
gen12-02-egito-e-lot.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-02-egito-e-lot.objective: What does Lot's choice reveal about what we value?
gen12-02-egito-e-lot.hookNote: Hunger takes Abram to Egypt; later, he and Lot part ways—Abram keeps the promise, Lot chooses the plain.

gen12-03-melquisedeque.title: War and Melchizedek
gen12-03-melquisedeque.intro: Abram rescues Lot and meets Melchizedek, king of Salem — bread, wine and blessing in the name of the Most High God.
gen12-03-melquisedeque.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-03-melquisedeque.objective: Why does Abram refuse Sodom's goods?
gen12-03-melquisedeque.hookNote: Abram rescues Lot and meets Melchizedek, king of Salem — bread, wine and blessing in the name of the Most High God.

gen12-04-alianca-estrelas.title: The alliance of stars
gen12-04-alianca-estrelas.intro: Abram believes—and it is imputed to him as righteousness. God severs covenant: offspring like the stars.
gen12-04-alianca-estrelas.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-04-alianca-estrelas.objective: What does “Abram believed in the Lord” mean?
gen12-04-alianca-estrelas.hookNote: Abram believes—and it is imputed to him as righteousness. God severs covenant: offspring like the stars.

gen12-05-agar-ismael.title: Hagar and Ishmael
gen12-05-agar-ismael.intro: Impatience creates a shortcut: Hagar conceives Ishmael. God sees the afflicted one — El-Roi.
gen12-05-agar-ismael.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-05-agar-ismael.objective: What happens when we try to “help” God’s promise?
gen12-05-agar-ismael.hookNote: Impatience creates a shortcut: Hagar conceives Ishmael. God sees the afflicted one — El-Roi.

gen12-06-circuncisao.title: New names and circumcision
gen12-06-circuncisao.intro: Abram becomes Abraham; Sarai becomes Sara. Circumcision seals the covenant—and Isaac is announced.
gen12-06-circuncisao.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-06-circuncisao.objective: Why does God change the names of Abram and Sarai?
gen12-06-circuncisao.hookNote: Abram becomes Abraham; Sarai becomes Sara. Circumcision seals the covenant—and Isaac is announced.

gen12-07-sodoma.title: Visitors and Sodom
gen12-07-sodoma.intro: Three visitors; Abraham intercedes. Sodom falls—and Lot is taken away. God's justice and mercy meet.
gen12-07-sodoma.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-07-sodoma.objective: What does Abraham's intercession teach about praying for others?
gen12-07-sodoma.hookNote: Three visitors; Abraham intercedes. Sodom falls—and Lot is taken away. God's justice and mercy meet.

gen12-08-isaque-nasce.title: Isaac is born
gen12-08-isaque-nasce.intro: In God's time, Sarah laughs with joy: Isaac is born. Abimelech and the covenant show that God keeps the promise.
gen12-08-isaque-nasce.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-08-isaque-nasce.objective: How does Isaac's birth confirm God's faithfulness?
gen12-08-isaque-nasce.hookNote: In God's time, Sarah laughs with joy: Isaac is born. Abimelech and the covenant show that God keeps the promise.

gen12-09-moria.title: Moriah—the offered son
gen12-09-moria.intro: The ultimate test: offering Isaac. On the mountain, God provides the lamb. Jehovah-Jireh.
gen12-09-moria.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-09-moria.objective: What does Abraham learn about God in Moriah?
gen12-09-moria.hookNote: The ultimate test: offering Isaac. On the mountain, God provides the lamb. Jehovah-Jireh.

gen12-boss-abraao.title: Challenge: Abraham
gen12-boss-abraao.intro: From the call to Moriah — one faith, covenant and provision on Abraham’s journey.
gen12-boss-abraao.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-boss-abraao.objective: What is the thread that connects the calling, the covenant and Moriah?
gen12-boss-abraao.hookNote: From the call to Moriah — one faith, covenant and provision on Abraham’s journey.

gen12-10-rebeca.title: Isaac and Rebekah
gen12-10-rebeca.intro: Sara rests; the servant prays at the well — and Rebekah appears. The line of promise continues into the next generation.
gen12-10-rebeca.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-10-rebeca.objective: How does the servant's prayer show dependence on God?
gen12-10-rebeca.hookNote: Sara rests; the servant prays at the well — and Rebekah appears. The line of promise continues into the next generation.

gen12-11-esaue-jaco.title: Esau and Jacob
gen12-11-esaue-jaco.intro: Two people in the womb. Isaac in Gerar; birthright exchanged for a plate; blessing taken in error.
gen12-11-esaue-jaco.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-11-esaue-jaco.objective: What does Jacob seek—and at what cost?
gen12-11-esaue-jaco.hookNote: Two people in the womb. Isaac in Gerar; birthright exchanged for a plate; blessing taken in error.

gen12-12-betel.title: Bethel​—The Ladder
gen12-12-betel.intro: On the run, Jacob dreams: stairs between heaven and earth. God renews the promise—this is Bethel.
gen12-12-betel.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-12-betel.objective: What does the ladder dream reveal about the presence of God?
gen12-12-betel.hookNote: On the run, Jacob dreams: stairs between heaven and earth. God renews the promise—this is Bethel.

gen12-13-labao.title: Laban, Leah and Rachel
gen12-13-labao.intro: Years in Haran: deception by Laban, Leah and Rachel, children of the tribes — and the flight back to the land.
gen12-13-labao.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-13-labao.objective: How does God work even in the midst of rivalry and waiting?
gen12-13-labao.hookNote: Years in Haran: deception by Laban, Leah and Rachel, children of the tribes — and the flight back to the land.

gen12-14-peniel.title: Peniel — fight and new name
gen12-14-peniel.intro: Jacob fights and turns Israel; finds Esau; the family returns to Bethel — wounds and renewal on the way.
gen12-14-peniel.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-14-peniel.objective: What changes in Jacob after Peniel?
gen12-14-peniel.hookNote: Jacob fights and turns Israel; finds Esau; the family returns to Bethel — wounds and renewal on the way.

gen12-boss-jaco.title: Challenge: Isaac and Jacob
gen12-boss-jaco.intro: From rivalry to new name — unite the thread of Isaac, Jacob and the promise.
gen12-boss-jaco.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-boss-jaco.objective: How does God transform Jacob along the journey?
gen12-boss-jaco.hookNote: From rivalry to new name — unite the thread of Isaac, Jacob and the promise.

gen12-15-sonhos.title: Dreams and betrayal
gen12-15-sonhos.intro: Tunic, dreams and jealousy: José is sold. Judah and Tamar also reveal the messianic line in the midst of failure.
gen12-15-sonhos.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-15-sonhos.objective: Where do you see God in the midst of betrayal and family failure?
gen12-15-sonhos.hookNote: Tunic, dreams and jealousy: José is sold. Judah and Tamar also reveal the messianic line in the midst of failure.

gen12-16-potifar.title: Potiphar and prison
gen12-16-potifar.intro: Joseph prospers in Potiphar's house—and is falsely accused. In prison, the Lord remains with him.
gen12-16-potifar.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-16-potifar.objective: What does José's integrity cost—and is it worth?
gen12-16-potifar.hookNote: Joseph prospers in Potiphar's house—and is falsely accused. In prison, the Lord remains with him.

gen12-17-farao.title: From prison to palace
gen12-17-farao.intro: Dreams of the butler, the baker and Pharaoh. Joseph interprets — and is placed over Egypt.
gen12-17-farao.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-17-farao.objective: How does the gift of Joseph serve the salvation of many?
gen12-17-farao.hookNote: Dreams of the butler, the baker and Pharaoh. Joseph interprets — and is placed over Egypt.

gen12-18-irmaos.title: The brothers before Joseph
gen12-18-irmaos.intro: Famine brings the brothers to Egypt. Joseph tests their hearts — and Benjamin enters the scene.
gen12-18-irmaos.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-18-irmaos.objective: What does Joseph try to see in his brothers?
gen12-18-irmaos.hookNote: Famine brings the brothers to Egypt. Joseph tests their hearts — and Benjamin enters the scene.

gen12-19-revelacao.title: José reveals himself
gen12-19-revelacao.intro: “I am José.” Crying, forgiveness and invitation: God sent me forward to preserve lives.
gen12-19-revelacao.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-19-revelacao.objective: How does Joseph interpret suffering in the light of God?
gen12-19-revelacao.hookNote: “I am José.” Crying, forgiveness and invitation: God sent me forward to preserve lives.

gen12-20-egito-bencao.title: Jacob in Egypt and the blessing
gen12-20-egito-bencao.intro: The family goes down to Egypt. Jacob blesses his children; Joseph mourns his father — and says: God means evil for good.
gen12-20-egito-bencao.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-20-egito-bencao.objective: How does Genesis end by pointing to hope?
gen12-20-egito-bencao.hookNote: The family goes down to Egypt. Jacob blesses his children; Joseph mourns his father — and says: God means evil for good.

gen12-boss-jose.title: Challenge: José
gen12-boss-jose.intro: From the cistern to the palace — unite dreams, suffering, forgiveness and providence.
gen12-boss-jose.centralInsight: What does this excerpt reveal about God’s faithfulness?
gen12-boss-jose.objective: What is the central theme of Joseph's story?
gen12-boss-jose.hookNote: From the cistern to the palace — unite dreams, suffering, forgiveness and providence.

exo-01-opressao.title: The people in Egypt
exo-01-opressao.intro: Genesis ends with Israel in Egypt. Exodus begins centuries later: a new pharaoh enslaves the people. God hears the cry of His people.
exo-01-opressao.objective: What does Pharaoh's fear reveal about human power?
exo-01-opressao.hookNote: Israel grew under blessing; Pharaoh's political fear turned to oppression. The cry of the people rises to God.

exo-02-moises.title: The Call of Moses
exo-02-moises.intro: God calls Moses at the burning bush. He hesitates, but God promises to be with him.
exo-02-moises.objective: Why does God reveal the Name before sending Moses?
exo-02-moises.hookNote: In the desert, God calls a fugitive. The holy presence (bush) and the revealed Name support the mission.

exo-03-pragas.title: The ten plagues
exo-03-pragas.intro: God sends plagues on Egypt so that Pharaoh will free Israel. Each plague shows God's power over the gods of Egypt.
exo-03-pragas.objective: What do the plagues teach about who God is?
exo-03-pragas.hookNote: Plagues confront the idols of Egypt. It is judgment and revelation: YHWH is the Lord.

exo-04-pascoa.title: Easter
exo-04-pascoa.intro: God institutes Easter: the blood of the lamb on the lintel would protect the houses. It is a liberation memorial.
exo-04-pascoa.objective: Why does the memorial require blood and sharing?
exo-04-pascoa.hookNote: Easter unites sacrifice, protection and memorial. Israel leaves by the grace of the lamb.

exo-05-mar.title: The Red Sea
exo-05-mar.intro: Pharaoh persecutes Israel. God opens the sea, the people pass on dry land and the Egyptians are defeated.
exo-05-mar.objective: What does “the Lord will fight for you” mean today?
exo-05-mar.hookNote: Between Egypt and the sea, Israel learns: salvation is from the Lord, not from one's own strength.

exo-boss-01.title: Challenge: Leaving Egypt
exo-boss-01.intro: Time to prove you understand the grand narrative of liberation. This challenge covers oppression, Moses, plagues, and the Red Sea.
exo-boss-01.objective: What is the thread that connects the bush, Easter and the Red Sea?
exo-boss-01.hookNote: This challenge unites oppression, calling, Easter and the sea. The thread is God's liberating faithfulness.

exo-06-mana.title: Manna in the desert
exo-06-mana.intro: Free from Egypt, the people face hunger. God sustains — and teaches confidence day by day.
exo-06-mana.objective: In what area do you need to rely on providing one day at a time?
exo-06-mana.hookNote: Hunger in the desert becomes a classroom. God sustains — and forms daily confidence.

exo-07-sinai.title: Arrival at Sinai
exo-07-sinai.intro: Three months after leaving, Israel camps in front of the mountain. God calls them to be priestly people.
exo-07-sinai.objective: What changes if your faith is a priestly vocation, and not just a private privilege?
exo-07-sinai.hookNote: Liberation has a destination: a people who belong to God and serve before the nations.

exo-08-mandamentos.title: The Ten Commandments
exo-08-mandamentos.intro: At Sinai, God speaks. The commandments are not empty weight—they are the way of the covenant.
exo-08-mandamentos.objective: Which “other gods” compete with the Lord in your routine?
exo-08-mandamentos.hookNote: Before “you shall not have”, comes “I took it from you”. The law walks on liberation.

exo-09-bezerro.title: The golden calf
exo-09-bezerro.intro: While Moses is on the mountain, the people ask for a visible god. The covenant almost breaks — and Moses intercedes.
exo-09-bezerro.objective: Where have you asked for a “god” faster and more visible than the Lord?
exo-09-bezerro.hookNote: A demora revela o coração. A manageable idol is preferred to a holy and free God.

exo-10-tabernaculo.title: The tabernacle
exo-10-tabernaculo.intro: God not only liberates — he desires to dwell among the people. The tabernacle is a presence on the path.
exo-10-tabernaculo.objective: Do you treat faith as an escape from Egypt or as life with God on the path?
exo-10-tabernaculo.hookNote: The objective is not just to leave Egypt — it is God in the middle of the camp.

exo-boss-02.title: Challenge: Alliance in the desert
exo-boss-02.intro: Manna, Sinai, commandments, fall and tabernacle — liberation continues in the formation of the people.
exo-boss-02.objective: Does your journey seek only miracles on the way out — or glory in the middle?
exo-boss-02.hookNote: From manna to glory: the desert ends this arc with God dwelling in the middle.

evg-01-encarnacao.title: The Word became flesh
evg-01-encarnacao.intro: The Gospels begin with a radical statement: God enters history in Jesus.
evg-01-encarnacao.objective: What changes if Jesus is the Word made flesh?
evg-01-encarnacao.hookNote: The Gospels open with God entering the story. Jesus is not just a teacher — he is the eternal Word.

evg-02-batismo.title: The baptism of Jesus
evg-02-batismo.intro: Jesus is baptized by John. Heaven opens — Beloved Son, Spirit and public mission.
evg-02-batismo.objective: Why does the Father's voice matter at the beginning of the ministry?
evg-02-batismo.hookNote: Baptism marks the public beginning: Father, Son and Spirit present in the mission.

evg-03-tentacao.title: The temptation in the desert
evg-03-tentacao.intro: After baptism, Jesus is taken to the desert. He responds to temptation with Scripture.
evg-03-tentacao.objective: How does the Word sustain you in temptation?
evg-03-tentacao.hookNote: In the desert, Jesus is faithful where Israel failed. Scripture is His defense.

evg-boss-01.title: Challenge: The Beginning
evg-boss-01.intro: Unite birth, baptism and temptation: who Jesus is and how the ministry begins.
evg-boss-01.objective: What thread unites incarnation, baptism and temptation?
evg-boss-01.hookNote: From the Cradle to the Desert: Identity and Obedience Open the Ministry.

evg-04-sermao.title: The Beatitudes
evg-04-sermao.intro: On the mountain, Jesus announces the Kingdom in an inverted way: the poor, the meek and the persecuted are blessed.
evg-04-sermao.objective: What do the Beatitudes challenge in you?
evg-04-sermao.hookNote: The Sermon on the Mount inverts values: the Kingdom begins in dependence on God.

evg-05-parabolas.title: The parables of the Kingdom
evg-05-parabolas.intro: Jesus teaches in parables: seeds, treasures and doors — the Kingdom grows in surprising ways.
evg-05-parabolas.objective: What soil describes your heart today?
evg-05-parabolas.hookNote: Parables reveal and hide: the Kingdom grows through the Word received.

evg-06-milagres.title: Signs and compassion
evg-06-milagres.intro: Miracles are not an empty spectacle: they reveal the King’s authority and mercy.
evg-06-milagres.objective: How does the power of Jesus combine with compassion?
evg-06-milagres.hookNote: Signs reveal the compassionate King: power in the service of care.

evg-boss-02.title: Challenge: Teaching and Signs
evg-boss-02.intro: Unite beatitudes, parables and miracles: how the Kingdom reveals itself.
evg-boss-02.objective: How does the Kingdom show itself in teaching and signs?
evg-boss-02.hookNote: Beatitudes, parables and miracles paint the same Kingdom.

evg-07-ceia.title: The last supper
evg-07-ceia.intro: On the night he was betrayed, Jesus instituted the new covenant in His blood.
evg-07-ceia.objective: What does it mean to participate in supper with conscience?
evg-07-ceia.hookNote: At supper, Jesus interprets His death: body given, blood of the covenant.

evg-08-cruz.title: The cross
evg-08-cruz.intro: Jesus is crucified. The Gospels show abandonment, mockery—and fulfillment of Scripture.
evg-08-cruz.objective: What does the cross say about the value of your life before God?
evg-08-cruz.hookNote: The cross is no accident: it is love that pays the ransom.

evg-09-ressurreicao.title: He is resurrected
evg-09-ressurreicao.intro: The empty tomb and the apparitions change everything: death does not have the last word.
evg-09-ressurreicao.objective: How does the resurrection change your mission today?
evg-09-ressurreicao.hookNote: The empty tomb launches the mission: the living Lord sends His people.

evg-boss-final.title: Final Challenge: Gospels
evg-boss-final.intro: From the incarnate Word to the resurrected King — unite the thread of the four Gospels.
evg-boss-final.objective: What is the bow you carry from the Gospels?
evg-boss-final.hookNote: The four Gospels tell an arc: coming, cross and victory.

mt-01-rei-prometido.title: The Promised King
mt-01-rei-prometido.intro: Matthew presents Jesus as the promised Messiah, Son of David and King who came to fulfill the Scriptures.
mt-01-rei-prometido.centralInsight: Genealogy links Jesus to Abraham and David. His birth by the Holy Spirit fulfills Emmanuel's promise: God with us.
mt-01-rei-prometido.hookNote: Matthew presents Jesus as the promised Messiah, Son of David and King who came to fulfill the Scriptures.

mt-02-reino-ensino.title: The Kingdom and its teaching
mt-02-reino-ensino.intro: Jesus teaches the life of the Kingdom: disciples depend on the Father, practice justice and listen to his words.
mt-02-reino-ensino.centralInsight: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus does not offer a way to deserve God; it describes the lives of those who belong to the Kingdom and depend on it.
mt-02-reino-ensino.hookNote: Jesus teaches the life of the Kingdom: disciples depend on the Father, practice justice and listen to his words.

mt-03-autoridade.title: King's Authority
mt-03-autoridade.intro: Jesus demonstrates authority over illness, demons, nature and sin, calling people to follow him in faith.
mt-03-autoridade.centralInsight: The miracles in Matthew are not tricks: they reveal the authority of the Messiah and point to his compassion and his Kingdom.
mt-03-autoridade.hookNote: Jesus demonstrates authority over illness, demons, nature and sin, calling people to follow him in faith.

mt-04-cruz-vitoria.title: The cross and victory
mt-04-cruz-vitoria.intro: The King serves, gives his life for sinners, resurrects bodily and sends disciples to all nations.
mt-04-cruz-vitoria.centralInsight: Jesus' death is voluntary and sacrificial. His resurrection confirms his victory and substantiates the mission of the church.
mt-04-cruz-vitoria.hookNote: The King serves, gives his life for sinners, resurrects bodily and sends disciples to all nations.

mt-boss-revisao.title: Challenge: The King and his Kingdom
mt-boss-revisao.intro: Review Jesus, the promised King, his teaching, his authority, his death and resurrection.
mt-boss-revisao.centralInsight: What does Jesus/the church reveal here?
mt-boss-revisao.hookNote: Review Jesus, the promised King, his teaching, his authority, his death and resurrection.

mc-01-servo-autoridade.title: The Servant with Authority
mc-01-servo-autoridade.intro: Mark presents Jesus in action: the Son of God announces the Kingdom and serves with authority over evil and illness.
mc-01-servo-autoridade.centralInsight: From the beginning, Jesus calls people to abandon sin and trust in the good news of the Kingdom of God.
mc-01-servo-autoridade.hookNote: Mark presents Jesus in action: the Son of God announces the Kingdom and serves with authority over evil and illness.

mc-02-caminho-cruz.title: The way of the cross
mc-02-caminho-cruz.intro: When Peter recognizes Jesus as Christ, Jesus teaches that following him includes denying himself, taking up the cross, and serving.
mc-02-caminho-cruz.centralInsight: Jesus corrects expectations of glory without suffering. He is the Christ who suffers, and his disciples follow him on the path of service.
mc-02-caminho-cruz.hookNote: When Peter recognizes Jesus as Christ, Jesus teaches that following him includes denying himself, taking up the cross, and serving.

mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao.title: The Servant wins through the cross
mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao.intro: Jesus enters Jerusalem, gives himself up according to God's plan, dies and is resurrected, overcoming death.
mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao.centralInsight: On the cross, the suffering Servant reveals his identity. The empty tomb announces that death did not have the last word.
mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao.hookNote: Jesus enters Jerusalem, gives himself up according to God's plan, dies and is resurrected, overcoming death.

mc-boss-revisao.title: Challenge: The Mighty Servant
mc-boss-revisao.intro: Review the announcement of the Kingdom, the discipleship that serves and the victory of Jesus on the cross.
mc-boss-revisao.centralInsight: What does Jesus/the church reveal here?
mc-boss-revisao.hookNote: Review the announcement of the Kingdom, the discipleship that serves and the victory of Jesus on the cross.

lc-01-salvador-humilde.title: The Savior of the humble
lc-01-salvador-humilde.intro: Luke shows Jesus arriving in humility and bringing good news to the poor, sinners and people left on the margins.
lc-01-salvador-humilde.centralInsight: The birth of Jesus is announced to shepherds. Luke highlights the joy of salvation and the grace of God that reaches the humble.
lc-01-salvador-humilde.objective: Birth and good news to the poor
lc-01-salvador-humilde.hookNote: Luke shows Jesus arriving in humility and bringing good news to the poor, sinners and people left on the margins.

lc-02-misericordia.title: The mercy you seek
lc-02-misericordia.intro: Luke highlights God's joy in seeking out sinners and calls his children to love their neighbors mercifully.
lc-02-misericordia.centralInsight: The parables of the sheep, the coin and the lost son reveal the heart of God. Jesus welcomes sinners and calls them to repentance.
lc-02-misericordia.hookNote: Luke highlights God's joy in seeking out sinners and calls his children to love their neighbors mercifully.

lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.title: Heading to Jerusalem
lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.intro: Jesus walks resolutely toward Jerusalem, teaching prayer, humility, service, and the cost of following him.
lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.centralInsight: The trip to Jerusalem organizes much of Luke. Jesus knows that his mission involves suffering, but he remains obedient to the Father's plan.
lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.hookNote: Jesus walks resolutely toward Jerusalem, teaching prayer, humility, service, and the cost of following him.

lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.title: The victory of Christ
lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.intro: Jesus suffers and dies as the promised Christ, resurrects and opens the understanding of the disciples to the Scriptures.
lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.centralInsight: Christ was not defeated by the cross. His suffering and his glory fulfill God's plan announced in the Scriptures.
lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.hookNote: Jesus suffers and dies as the promised Christ, resurrects and opens the understanding of the disciples to the Scriptures.

lc-boss-revisao.title: Challenge: The Savior who seeks

lc-boss-revisao.centralInsight: What does Jesus/the church reveal here?
lc-boss-revisao.hookNote: Review the good news for the humble, mercy, the way to Jerusalem and the victory of Christ.

jo-01-verbo-sinais.title: The Word and the signs
jo-01-verbo-sinais.intro: John announces Jesus as the eternal Word made flesh. His signs reveal his glory and invite faith.
jo-01-verbo-sinais.centralInsight: John begins before creation: the eternal Son was with God and is God. By becoming man, he reveals the Father without ceasing to be God.
jo-01-verbo-sinais.objective: Jesus reveals the glory of the Father
jo-01-verbo-sinais.hookNote: John announces Jesus as the eternal Word made flesh. His signs reveal his glory and invite faith.

jo-02-eu-sou.title: I am
jo-02-eu-sou.intro: Jesus uses profound images to reveal his identity: he is light, door, good shepherd, resurrection, way and life.
jo-02-eu-sou.centralInsight: I Am statements show that Jesus is sufficient for his people and share echoes of God's name revealed in the Old Testament.
jo-02-eu-sou.hookNote: Jesus uses profound images to reveal his identity: he is light, door, good shepherd, resurrection, way and life.

jo-03-adeus-espirito.title: Remain in me
jo-03-adeus-espirito.intro: Before the cross, Jesus consoles his disciples, commands sacrificial love, and promises the Holy Spirit to strengthen them.
jo-03-adeus-espirito.centralInsight: In his farewell speeches, Jesus does not leave his disciples orphans. The Spirit applies the work of Christ and leads them into the truth.
jo-03-adeus-espirito.hookNote: Before the cross, Jesus consoles his disciples, commands sacrificial love, and promises the Holy Spirit to strengthen them.

jo-04-cruz-tome.title: The Crucified and the Resurrected
jo-04-cruz-tome.intro: Jesus gives his life out of love, resurrects and calls Thomas — and all readers — to believe in him as Lord and God.
jo-04-cruz-tome.centralInsight: John shows the cross as the hour of Jesus' glorification. The Resurrected One appears to the disciples and transforms doubt into a confession of faith.
jo-04-cruz-tome.hookNote: Jesus gives his life out of love, resurrects and calls Thomas — and all readers — to believe in him as Lord and God.

jo-boss-revisao.hookNote: Review the Word made flesh, the signs, the I Am statements, the Spirit, and faith in the Resurrected One.

ato-06-gentios.intro: Cornelius and Peter: the Spirit breaks down barriers. The gospel is not the property of a people.
ato-06-gentios.objective: What cultural or social boundaries do I still treat as too “impure” for the gospel?

ato-07-missoes.title: Mission from Antioch
ato-07-missoes.intro: The fasting church sends. The word goes out among the nations—with opposition and joy.

ato-07-missoes.objective: Does my community only receive — or does it also send?

ato-08-roma.title: To Rome
ato-08-roma.intro: Arrested, but not silent. The gospel reaches the heart of the Empire—unhindered.

ato-08-roma.hookNote: The book ends not with triumphal release, but with testimony in custody. Rome is not the end of history — it is a sign that the 1:8 map is moving forward…

ato-boss-02.hookNote: Review the breakthrough: Saul, Gentiles, sending and witnessing in Rome.
